builds.howItPlays: You set cheap cards like Evelynn, Entrancing face down for a rune each, then play them for free in the middle of a fight, with surprises like Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror, a 4-cost unit you can drop at any time onto a battlefield where you already have units. Every combat you win draws you a card, so each fight your opponent walks into refills your hand.
builds.whyYou: You like keeping your opponent guessing, with a few face-down cards on the table and runes held back, so any attack they make could run into something they didn't see coming. You'd rather set a trap than win a straight race: you put solid units on the battlefields, then turn the fight at the last second. You don't mind thinking a turn ahead about which runes to spend and which cards to hide. If you'd rather win fights with surprises than with sheer size, this Draven suits you.
builds.ratingNotes: Scored decks (tools.ts style: Tempo 6/6.5/6.5/4, mean of 3; labels Tempo, Tempo, Tempo): https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/4d431fc2-210e-4ebc-8456-225db6f64ddc (arko, Draven Post-Ban Vendetta, guide, edited 2026-09-18) 6/6/6.5/4.5; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/93271c80-faba-4662-8bc5-74c5cf183a3d (unawares, Post Ban Draven) 6.5/6.5/6.5/3; https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/c1bce7a8-1155-415f-9917-2be1a7dcc211 (Alessandro Tassini, DRAVEN) 6/6.5/6/4.5. All three are legal. Adjustments: stance +0.5 on all three, given as 'Legend only pays off when you start and win fights'. That reason is loose because the Legend also draws on defensive wins; what it means is that these lists go looking for fights. Complexity +0.5: Forge of the Fluft gives the Legend an equip ability to time, and Star Spring rewards choosing where units are played. Variance -0.5 to -1: the Legend draws on every combat win, and Zaun Warrens loots on conquer or Grove of the God-Willow draws on hold. Deciding cards. Pace: about 9 two-cost units (Evelynn, Overzealous Fan, Tideturner, Teemo) and only 1-2 cards costing 5+ (Draven, Showboat; Ferrous Forerunner). Stance: 25-26 units and pressure against about 13 answers (Falling Star, Rebuke, Gust, Star-Crossed, Overzealous Fan, Vex), with 15-18 reaction-speed cards pulling it off Aggro. Complexity: 10 Hidden cards, Quick-Draw Spinning Axe, Ambush Kha'Zix and Reaction Rengar, Pouncing; the timing sits in when to set and flip cards, not in engines. Variance: no luck or swing cards and removal that always does its job; low 3-of density in two lists keeps it from dropping further. Scorer and judged labels differ once: the unawares list (scorer Aggro, judged Tempo, 17 reactive cards). No 2+ formula/judgment gaps. Legend ability: when you win a combat, draw 1 (you win if only your units remain). Also played: Kai'Sa Draven https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/8be505d5-2fc9-4f26-b05f-286e44bd67cb (Tempo 5.5/6/6/4), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/a2a34422-c8c8-4d04-889b-6a5aada08a95 (Midrange 6/6.5/5.5/4.5), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/ef1fed3d-6531-4fda-8a3b-2e2872f96307 (Midrange 6/6.5/5.5/4); Hold Draven https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/f35329ce-d207-42bd-88aa-3fc2fde3a8aa (pre-ban, Midrange 5.5/5.5/6.5/4), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/b3733582-8be2-4086-bb47-261fae1c104d (Midrange 5.5/6/6/4); Stompy Draven https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/5b655777-2db3-4e34-80bb-a1a28a69ad57 (Midrange 6/7/6/4). Confidence: low. Change 2026-09-25: relabelled Midrange to Tempo and moved from 5/5.5/7/6.5 to 6/6.5/6.5/4. Variance moved 2.5, mostly because the old reading leaned on Stacked Deck-era lists and on the idea that Hidden cards are luck. The rubric scores face-down cards as timing (Complexity), not chance. The deckListUrl moved from the Singapore RQ list (a4cc19aa, 3 Stacked Deck, banned 2026-09-18) to arko's post-ban list. The guideUrls from the old Build (hextech, riftbound.zone, riftbound.gg and the three pre-ban deck pages) were dropped because they describe pre-ban Stacked Deck lists. The picks' lead agent chose this style over Kai'Sa Draven, which has more evidence (6.1 to 5.7) but mostly from pre-ban lists. Outside sources (riftbound.gg, riftbound.zone) called pre-ban Draven Midrange, while hextech leaned tempo. The Kai'Sa-style decks score 1 or less away on every Axis, so either label is defensible. Reviewer check: arko's on-page guide loads lazily and I read only its summary ('Typical Draven, cheat combats, win with card advantage').
